raw_segments.text: Accordingly, we went with Polemarchus to his house, and there we found his brothers Lygias
and Euthydmus, and with them Thrasimachus the Chalcedonian, Charmin tides the Peanian
and Claytofen the son of Aristonimus.
There too was Cephalus the father of Polemarchus, whom I had not seen for a long time, and I
He was seated on a cushioned chair, and had a garland on his head, for he had been sacrificing
in the court, and there were some other chairs in the room arranged in a semi-circle, upon
which we sat down by him.
He saluted me eagerly, and then he said.
